REST API authentication and conventions

Bearer authentication, trusted-header deployments, project scoping, CSRF, envelopes, pagination, request ids, and error shapes.

DeveloperReferenceGA
PrerequisitesA running CALIBER deployment
Reviewed 2026-10-15 · current main branch docs contract

These pages document the HTTP contract itself: the headers you send, the envelopes you receive, and the failure shapes you should handle before you build your own client.

Authentication modes#

CALIBER supports three identity patterns, but only two make sense for direct programmatic use:

ModeHow it worksUse it when
Bearer tokenAuthorization: Bearer <token>normal automation and external integrations
Trusted headerX-CALIBER-User: <user> plus optional X-CALIBER-Proxy-Secretonly behind a trusted identity proxy in trusted_header deployments
Browser sessionsession cookie plus CSRF tokenbrowser traffic and same-origin UI requests, not headless automation

Personal access tokens (the calpat_ prefix) are the default automation credential. Trusted headers carry no proof by themselves and are ignored in the default session deployment mode.

A token's scopes are a ceiling: its effective authority is what it requested intersected with what its owner holds at request time, and a token cannot be issued with a scope its issuer lacks (403). A token can also be bound to one project by passing project_id when it is created (POST /auth/tokens); the issuer must already be able to see that project. A bound token that names a different project in X-CALIBER-Project or in the URL is refused with 403, and a bound token that names no project acts in its bound project. Unbound tokens, sessions and trusted-header identities are unaffected. The Workspace import routes (/projects/{project_id}/revision-imports) additionally refuse a personal access token that is not bound to that project; session callers are not affected.

Core headers#

HeaderMeaning
Authorization: Bearer <token>Personal access token or session token
X-CALIBER-Project: <project_id>Active project/workspace scope
X-CALIBER-CSRF: <token>Required on POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE when CSRF enforcement is enabled (it is off by default)
X-Request-Id: <id>Optional caller-supplied correlation id; CALIBER also returns request ids on responses and errors
Accept: application/jsonPreferred for management API calls

Example:

curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-CALIBER-Project: $CALIBER_PROJECT" \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/workflows"

CSRF#

CSRF enforcement is off by default (CALIBER_CSRF_ENABLED), and GET /csrf then answers enabled: false. When a deployment turns it on, every POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE needs the header, except GET /csrf itself and the GitHub webhook route. That includes bearer-token calls: the middleware does not exempt them. The tokens are bound to the caller's identity and expire (CALIBER_CSRF_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS), and a missing or invalid one is a 403. The SDK fetches a token and replays the write once when it sees that failure.

Fetch a token with:

curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALIBER_TOKEN" \
  "$CALIBER_BASE_URL/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber/csrf"

The response carries enabled, token and ttl_seconds. Echo the returned token in X-CALIBER-CSRF on the write request.

Response envelopes#

Most management API responses use the standard envelope:

{
  "data": {
    "workflow_id": "WF-123",
    "name": "release-governance"
  }
}

Lists usually live under data as well:

{
  "data": [
    {"workflow_id": "WF-123"},
    {"workflow_id": "WF-456"}
  ]
}

A few routes answer with a bare body instead of the envelope: GET /health returns {"status", "version", "db"} at the top level, and the OpenAPI documents are the raw document. GET /health answers 503 with status: "degraded" when the database probe fails. GET /readiness does use the envelope, and answers 503 (the body is still under data) when a required dependency is not ready; that includes a database that has not been migrated to the schema this release expects (run caliber-migrate) and an unreachable MLflow tracking server.

Pagination and list conventions#

Many list endpoints accept:

  • ?limit=<n> (default 500, at most 2000 on routes that share the common helper)
  • ?offset=<n>

Invalid values fall back to defaults rather than failing request parsing, so a consumer that cares about deterministic pagination should always send explicit values. Pagination is not one shape across the API: some routes take only limit, the audit log returns its own envelope, the event streams take after, and the Workspace routes (/projects/{project_id}/revisions, .../revision-imports and similar) use limit plus an opaque cursor and return next_cursor next to data.

Error shapes#

General route failures come back as:

{
  "detail": "forbidden",
  "status_code": 403
}

Some routes also set a machine-readable reason_code next to detail ({"detail": ..., "status_code": 409, "reason_code": "..."}). It is optional and additive: most routes do not set it yet, so treat its absence as normal and fall back to detail and the status code.

One code is always set: a route of an area that this deployment has turned off answers 404 with reason_code: feature_disabled, and detail names the variable that enables it. The preview and record-only areas (Aria, MCP servers and OpenAPI integrations, cookbooks, release-candidate signoff and Workspace releases) are off by default. Read features from GET /capabilities to check before you call, and treat this 404 as "not enabled here" rather than "no such record":

{
  "detail": "Aria assistant and plans is disabled in this deployment. Set CALIBER_FEATURE_ARIA=true to enable it.",
  "status_code": 404,
  "reason_code": "feature_disabled"
}

A 429 carries a Retry-After header. When MLflow is unreachable, the prompt routes and Apply answer 503 with a fixed message naming MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, and nothing was changed.

Validation failures use a structured 400 body:

{
  "detail": "request body validation failed",
  "status_code": 400,
  "errors": [
    {
      "loc": ["instructions"],
      "msg": "instructions must reference at least one evaluation variable",
      "type": "value_error"
    }
  ]
}

Your client should treat transport failures, HTTP failures, and validation failures as three different classes of problem.
